story: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price INFY to move about ±7.1%, roughly 1,075 to 1,240. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 58% of the time.

For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 1,200 (+4.2% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 1,100 (-4.5%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
INFY futures trade 6.0 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 5.9% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
INFY has actually been moving about 2.03% a day this past month: normal for it against the past year.

iv.simple: Options on INFY are priced for moves of about 1.92% a day. That is normal for INFY compared with the past year.
iv.analyst: 30-day constant-maturity ATM IV 30.4%: 52nd percentile of 1 year, 73rd of all days since 2019-01-01.

vrp.simple: Options are cheap compared with how much INFY has actually been moving: they price 30.4% a year while the last month realised 32.3%.
vrp.analyst: IV30 - RV21 = -1.8 vol points, 52nd percentile of the past year. Since 2019-01-01, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 62% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

term.simple: Longer-dated options on INFY cost more than near ones: the normal, calm shape.

skew.simple: Protection against a fall costs more than a bet on a rise, by 1.7 vol points. That gap is normal for INFY against the past year.
skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal -1.65 vol pts (front month), 50th percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

realised.simple: INFY has actually been moving about 2.03% a day this past month: normal for it against the past year.
realised.analyst: RV21 32.3% (56th percentile of the past year), RV5 42.7%, RV63 33.3%; RV5/RV63 compression at the 78th percentile.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 1,200 (+4.2% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 1,100 (-4.5%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.54; all-expiry OI PCR at the 23rd percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +1,326,800, puts +17,200 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.simple: INFY futures trade 6.0 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 5.9% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
futures.analyst: Near-month basis +6.0, annualised carry 5.9% (72nd percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 4.0%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Long build-up, Long build-up, Long build-up, Long build-up, Long unwinding. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.

move.simple: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price INFY to move about ±7.1%, roughly 1,075 to 1,240. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 58% of the time.
move.analyst: ATM straddle / forward = 7.14% (forward 1,157.3). Scored on 1,956 days since 2019-01-01 against the official close on each expiry; a straddle is the market's mean absolute move, so about 57% inside is what a fair price would give.

notes.text: INFY has used 17% of its market-wide position limit (the ban starts at 95%).
Lot size changes from 400 to 500 for the 2027-01-25 contracts (the exchange has already listed them so).
